question: Your team runs Claude Code with the -p flag in CI to rewrite calls to a deprecated logging API across many modules. Each rewrite receives a confidence score, and rewrites above a threshold merge without human review. The team now wants an ongoing measure of the error rate in these high-confidence rewrites, and it also wants to catch error patterns that nobody has seen yet. Which review plan best meets this goal?

options.text: Each week, have reviewers check a random sample of merged high-confidence rewrites, stratified by module and rewrite type, and track the error rate for each stratum.
options.reason: Stratified random sampling of high-confidence outputs gives an unbiased, ongoing error rate for each segment and can surface novel error patterns that no existing check targets.

options.text: Move all reviewer time to the rewrites below the threshold, because the labeled validation set already showed that rewrites above the threshold are accurate.
options.reason: Validation-set calibration sets thresholds but does not replace ongoing sampling of high-confidence outputs, so their error rate and novel error patterns would go unmeasured.

options.text: Each week, have reviewers check only the merged rewrites whose CI tests later fail, because a failing test is the clearest sign of a rewrite error.
options.reason: This sample is selected by an existing check, so it is biased and cannot measure the true error rate or reveal new error patterns that the tests do not catch.

options.text: Each month, have reviewers check the same fixed benchmark set of 50 high-confidence rewrites that was chosen once at launch, so that the results stay comparable from month to month.
options.reason: A fixed set is not a fresh random sample of new high-confidence rewrites, so it cannot measure the ongoing error rate or detect error patterns that appear later.
